A common workaround map a surface to a planar domain and uses a standard CNN, but existing surface-to-image representations either large area distortion or require multiple images to cover the entire shape. We propose a new representation of ball surfaces based on general deck cards. Instead of relying on a toric cover with a fixed set of cone points, our construction wraps a flat torus several times around the surface, so that each region with a low distortion appears somewhere in a single image. Since this image is seamless and periodic, convolution with circular padding is well defined, and off-the-shelf architectures apply with minimal modification. The predictions from the multiple copies of each surface point are then aggregated to the mesh again. Experiments with form segmentation and classification benchmarks show that the method meets or exceeds competing approaches while remaining simple and efficient.
